events.name: Pendine Sands Hot Rod Races
events.blurb: The UK's premier vintage hot rod meeting, run by the Vintage Hot Rod Association on the historic firm sands of Pendine. Two days of speed runs with pre-1949 cars and bikes reaching over 130 mph; free for spectators outside the pits.

events.name: Pendine Sands Races
events.blurb: Running event held directly on the firm beach at Pendine, offering 5k, 10k, Half Marathon and Marathon distances on the famous land-speed-record sands.

events.name: Babs Land Speed Record Centenary
events.when: one-off centenary on 27 April 2026, with Babs on display at the Museum of Land Speed from May 2026
events.blurb: Special centenary celebration marking 100 years since J.G. Parry-Thomas set the world land speed record at Pendine Sands in 1926. The legendary car 'Babs' returns to the beach and goes on display at the Museum of Land Speed.

events.name: The Laugharne Weekend
events.blurb: An intimate literary and arts festival in the nearby town of Laugharne (about 7 km from Pendine), celebrating the legacy of Dylan Thomas with leftfield literature, music and comedy from Welsh and international artists.

events.name: Bedruthan Christmas Fayre
events.when: annually late November (Sat-Sun) at Bedruthan Hotel & Spa, Mawgan Porth; 2025 edition was 22-23 November, 2026 dates not yet confirmed
events.blurb: Annual craft and gift fair at the Bedruthan Hotel & Spa in Mawgan Porth, featuring art, ceramics, textiles, jewellery, homewares and local food and drink stalls.

events.name: St Eval Church Flower Festival
events.when: annually, normally the last weekend in June, at St Eval Parish Church (about 3 km from the beach)
events.blurb: Long-running community flower festival at the historic Grade I listed St Eval Church, with floral displays created by local volunteers and home-made refreshments.

events.name: Falcon Fest
events.when: annually in June at The Falcon Inn, St Mawgan (about 5 km away); a weekend of live music, cider, ales and street food in the pub garden
events.blurb: A weekend music and drink festival held in the garden of The Falcon Inn in the village of St Mawgan, with live bands, local ciders and ales, and street food.

events.name: Boardmasters Festival
events.when: annually in August at Watergate Bay and Fistral Beach, Newquay (Watergate Bay is roughly 6 km from the beach)
events.blurb: Cornwall's largest music and surf festival, held on the cliffs above Watergate Bay near Newquay, with a major line-up of music acts plus surfing and skating competitions.

events.name: Bedruthan Live (RE:SET summer music series)
events.when: summer season at Bedruthan Steps campsite, Mawgan Porth, with an outdoor live music series alongside wellness workshops
events.blurb: Summer programme of outdoor live music at the Bedruthan Steps campsite in Mawgan Porth, accompanied by yoga, sound baths and wellness sessions in the tipi field.

events.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Cayman Cookout
events.when: annually mid-January at The Ritz-Carlton on Seven Mile Beach; 2026 edition 14-18 January
events.blurb: A world-renowned food and wine festival held at The Ritz-Carlton, Grand Cayman, directly on Seven Mile Beach, with celebrity-chef cooking demonstrations, tastings and beachside dinners.

events.name: Flowers Sea Swim
events.when: annually in June along Seven Mile Beach; 2026 edition 13 June
events.blurb: A one-mile open-water swim race along Seven Mile Beach drawing over 1,000 competitors, from recreational swimmers to Olympic-level athletes.

events.name: One Cayman Carnival (Batabano & CayMAS)
events.when: annually in May; 2026 unified Road Parade on Saturday 23 May (Junior Parade 2 May), through George Town ending at Public Beach on Seven Mile Beach
events.blurb: Grand Cayman's national carnival, in 2026 uniting Batabano and CayMAS into One Cayman Carnival, with soca music, mas bands, costumes and a road parade ending at Seven Mile Beach Public Beach.

events.name: Pirates Week Festival
events.when: annually in November (typically the second week)
events.blurb: The Cayman Islands' signature maritime-heritage festival featuring a mock pirate invasion, parades, street dancing, local food, sports, Heritage Days and fireworks across Grand Cayman.

events.name: Cayman Art Week
events.blurb: A week-long curated programme of gallery tours, open studios and exhibitions celebrating local visual artists across the Cayman Islands.

events.name: Cayman Islands Agricultural Show
events.when: annually on Ash Wednesday; 2026 edition 18 February
events.blurb: A long-running agricultural fair showcasing the islands' livestock, produce and local food alongside live music and arts and crafts.

events.name: Aberavon Beach Festival
events.blurb: An annual community festival on Aberavon Beach featuring live music, tribute acts, market stalls, beach games, a kids' festival and wellness activities over a summer weekend.

events.name: Aberavon Super Sprint Triathlon
events.blurb: A community super-sprint triathlon organised by Port Talbot Harriers, with a 400m pool swim, a 10km bike course and a 3km run along Aberavon Beach.

events.name: Aberavon Surf Lifesaving Club Junior Aquathlon
events.blurb: A junior swim-and-run aquathlon held on Aberavon Beach, run by Aberavon Surf Lifesaving Club in conjunction with Port Talbot Harriers and Welsh Triathlon.

events.name: Aberdeen Festival of the Sea
events.blurb: A citywide celebration of Aberdeen's maritime heritage with around 40 free and paid events; the Beach Esplanade hosts headline elements including the parade of sail and a grand finale. It runs in July, coinciding with the Tall Ships Races visit to the harbour.

events.name: Aberdeen parkrun
events.blurb: A free, timed 5km run, jog or walk held every Saturday morning along the Beach Esplanade at Aberdeen Beach. Open to all and run by volunteers.

events.name: City of Aberdeen Baker Hughes 10k Running Festival
events.blurb: A long-established 10k road race (with 2k and wheelchair options) based around Aberdeen Beach and harbour, starting on Beach Boulevard and running along the Beach Esplanade past the Beach Ballroom. First held in 1987.

events.name: Fishguard Folk Festival
events.blurb: A mostly free folk music festival held at venues across Fishguard including St Mary's Church and Theatr Gwaun, with concerts, sessions, workshops, ceilidh/twmpath, dance displays and guided walks. The 2026 line-up includes Alaw, Cynefin and Three Daft Monkeys.

events.name: Fishguard Multi-Sport Festival
events.blurb: A weekend of endurance running races around Fishguard, including a Half Marathon, a scenic 10K and a 5K aimed at first-time racers.

events.name: ABBAGwaun Festival
events.blurb: A three-day ABBA-themed festival in Fishguard (Abergwaun) featuring film screenings, live music, ABBA bingo, costume competitions and a parade.

events.name: Fishguard Bay Ocean Race
events.blurb: An annual downwind paddle/ski sea race starting at Goodwick Parrog and crossing roughly 17km of open water to finish on Newport Sands, now in its second decade.

events.name: The Big Retreat Festival
events.blurb: An annual wellbeing and music festival set in the village of Lawrenny within the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, combining live music, food, talks and outdoor experiences over the May bank holiday weekend.

events.name: Pembroke Music Festival
events.blurb: An annual six-day music festival anchored at Pembroke Town Hall, the nearest sizeable town to Barafundle Bay, featuring concerts and performances across the autumn week.

events.name: Fishguard Folk Festival
events.when: annually over the late May bank holiday (2026: 22-26 May)
events.blurb: A traditional folk music festival held across venues in Fishguard, Pembrokeshire, over the May bank holiday weekend with concerts, dancing and food.

events.name: Dartmouth Triathlon
events.blurb: An annual sprint and standard-distance triathlon organised by Sportiva Events, with the sea swim leg held in the waters of Blackpool Sands followed by a bike ride via Slapton and a run up Blackpool Valley. Open sea swims of 750m, 1500m and 3km are also held the evening before.

events.name: Tribal Clash
events.blurb: A two-day team fitness competition held on a purpose-built arena on Blackpool Sands beach, where teams of six tackle surprise functional challenges including running, swimming, hauling and carrying. It is one of the beach's flagship recurring events.

events.name: Apres Sea Saturdays
events.when: Saturday afternoons through the summer season
events.blurb: Recurring summer beach parties at Blackpool Sands with live music and DJs on Saturday afternoons, alongside the beach's regular Saturday morning live music and breakfast club sessions.

events.name: Pembroke Festival
events.blurb: A multi-day arts and community festival in the historic town of Pembroke, the nearest town to Broad Haven South, featuring live music, town-wide arts events, workshops, crafts and family activities.

events.name: Pembroke Music Festival
events.blurb: A competitive music festival held over several days at Pembroke Town Hall, with classes in singing, piano, strings and choir, masterclasses and a finale concert.

events.name: The Big Retreat Festival
events.blurb: A wellbeing, music and food festival held at Lawrenny within the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, combining live music, wellbeing sessions, food, talks and outdoor experiences.

events.name: Rye Bay Scallop Week
events.when: annually late February to early March (2026: 21 Feb - 1 Mar)
events.blurb: A week-long celebration of the local Rye Bay scallop catch with tasting menus, cooking classes, live music and wine pairings across the town's restaurants. Now in its 22nd year, it is one of East Sussex's most popular annual food events.

events.name: Rye International Jazz & Blues Festival
events.when: annually over the August Bank Holiday (2026: 28-31 Aug)
events.blurb: A boutique music festival held in venues across Rye, including St Mary's Church, featuring jazz, blues, soul, R&B, funk and world music with a mix of ticketed and free performances over the August Bank Holiday weekend.

events.name: Camber Kite Week
events.blurb: An annual kitesurfing gathering on the wide flats of Camber Sands organised by the local kitesurfing community, combining kitesurfing sessions with music, food and beachside camping.

events.name: Rye Arts Festival
events.blurb: Founded in 1972 and regarded as one of Britain's top small arts festivals, it offers a mix of musical, literary and theatrical events across the historic town of Rye near Camber Sands.

camp-bay-gibraltar.town: Gibraltar (Camp Bay is on the south-west tip of the Rock of Gibraltar)

events.name: Summer Nights - Summer Reggae Jam at Camp Bay
events.blurb: Camp Bay beach hosts a free open-air Reggae Jam as part of Gibraltar's Summer Nights programme, with live acts, sunset dancing and food stalls. In 2025 it ran on 7 August from 6:30pm to 11:00pm.

events.name: Gibraltar National Day
events.blurb: Gibraltar's biggest annual celebration, when the territory dresses in red and white for street parties, concerts and the release of thousands of red-and-white balloons. It commemorates the 1967 sovereignty referendum.

events.name: Gibraltar International Dance Festival
events.blurb: The 24th edition of Gibraltar's international dance festival runs 3-7 March 2026 at the John Mackintosh Hall Theatre, featuring over 250 dancers from Gibraltar, England, Italy, Spain and Albania.

events.name: Gibraltar Music Festival
events.blurb: Gibraltar's flagship music festival, traditionally held at the Alameda Botanical Gardens, drawing major international acts each year.

events.name: Walrus Dip (Boxing Day Swim)
events.blurb: An annual Boxing Day charity sea swim held on the dune-backed sands of Cefn Sidan beach at Pembrey Country Park, with fancy dress encouraged. The dip starts around 10:45am and attracts hundreds of swimmers and spectators.

events.name: Wales National Armed Forces Day 2026
events.blurb: Carmarthenshire hosts the Wales National Armed Forces Day 2026 at Pembrey Country Park, a family-friendly event for the public to show support for the Armed Forces community.

events.name: Pembrey Summer Feastival
events.blurb: A coastal food and music weekend at Pembrey Country Park, set between the woodland and the eight-mile Cefn Sidan beach, featuring nomadic cooks, family entertainment and a live music stage.

events.name: b-side Festival
events.blurb: A four-day contemporary arts festival staged across the Isle of Portland, featuring site-specific artworks, performances and creative encounters inspired by the island's landscape and community. The 2026 edition is themed 'That Other Place'.

events.name: Criccieth Festival (Gŵyl Criccieth)
events.blurb: An annual arts festival founded in 1990 celebrating music, culture and local heritage in Criccieth, featuring classical and folk concerts, literary talks and guided walks set against the backdrop of Cardigan Bay. It runs for around a week in mid-June.

events.name: Criccieth Food Slam
events.when: annually mid-June, closing weekend of the Criccieth Festival
events.blurb: A food festival held on the Criccieth esplanade beside the beach at the end of the Criccieth Festival week, with street food, beer, wine, live music and arts and crafts stalls.

events.name: Criccieth Fair and the Big Fair
events.blurb: Criccieth holds two traditional annual fairs dating back to the Victorian era, the first on 23 May and the larger 'Big Fair' on 29 June, with a funfair in the town.

events.name: Crosby parkrun
events.blurb: A free, timed 5km community run held every Saturday morning, starting near Crosby Leisure Centre and running along the promenade and Crosby Beach past Antony Gormley's 'Another Place' iron men sculptures.

events.name: Antony Gormley's 'Another Place'
events.blurb: One hundred life-size cast-iron figures by sculptor Antony Gormley are spread along almost 3km of Crosby Beach facing out to sea, a permanent free public artwork and the area's best-known visitor draw.
